title: Quantized L0C-to-UB transfers through a CvMutex handoff
surface: Tensor.requant(scale=, offset=).subblk(0) and Tensor.relu() on an L0C accumulator stored into a UB tensor; CvMutex(id, depth=, src_end_pipe=Pipe.FIX, dst_end_pipe=Pipe.V) with lock / ready / wait / free; GetSubBlockIdx() guarding the GM publication; a kernel(mode="mix") launch
study_for: The handoff, not the arithmetic, is the subject. `CvMutex` with `src_end_pipe=Pipe.FIX` and `dst_end_pipe=Pipe.V` bridges the cube fixpipe's store into UB and the vector side's read-back, in four beats. Both vector participants run all four; only subblock 0 writes GM, guarded by `GetSubBlockIdx()`. Dropping the beats in the participant that does not publish would leave the mutex unbalanced even though its output is never used.

`.subblk(0)` is required. The sources these seven cases came from omitted the rider even though their contract described a single subblock, and every conversion here carries it. A conversion without it is not the same instruction.

Byte quantization saturates twice, in an order that matters: scale, round to nearest even, clamp to the intermediate signed 9-bit range [-256, 255], add the offset, then saturate to the destination's range. An implementation that offset before the intermediate clamp, or skipped it, disagrees on the values the planted +8 and -8 rows produce.

The scale is truncated to FixP19 before it is applied, and the reference does that truncation explicitly with a `0xFFFFE000` mask. At 0.5 and 0.25 the truncation is the identity -- `check_domain` asserts exactly that -- so it changes no value here while stating the rule that would matter for a scale where it did.

The split case keeps the full L0C pitch. `l0c[0:16, :]` and `l0c[16:32, :]` are two conversions of one 32-row accumulator into two 16-row UB tensors, through two independent mutexes, and the GM output is written in two halves. Reading the wrong 16 rows duplicates one half and loses the other, which the whole-output comparison sees twice.
do_not_copy_when: You are leaving out the subblock rider. It is required, and its absence is not a simplification.
Your scale is not exact under FixP19. Then the truncation is part of the answer and needs its own reference; nothing here establishes how an arbitrary scale rounds.

Your operands are not small integers. The domain is [-8, 8] integral values, which is what makes the products and the FP16 results exact. Non-integral operands, infinities and NaNs are outside this example.

You want the two vector participants to do different work. Here both run the mutex beats and one publishes. A genuine split of the vector work across subblocks is a different ownership arrangement, and this example's guard would be the wrong shape for it.
